items.text: Uploads to the sync service keep stalling after a few failures. Can you look at the retry logic and tell me why?

tool.name: Read

items.text:
## Why the uploads stall

The retry loop in `uploadChunk` waits for the *previous* delay to finish **before** it computes the next one, so a burst of failures compounds instead of spreading out. Two things make it worse:

- the delay doubles on every attempt but is never capped
- the jitter is added to the delay instead of replacing part of it

### What I would change

1. Cap the delay at 30 seconds
2. Apply *full jitter*, a random value between zero and the capped delay
3. Stop after `maxAttempts` and surface the last error

Here is the shape of the fix:

```ts
export function nextDelay(attempt: number, base = 500, cap = 30_000): number {
  const ceiling = Math.min(cap, base * 2 ** attempt);
  return Math.floor(Math.random() * ceiling);
}
```

And how to check it from the command line:

```bash
npm test -- --grep "nextDelay"
node scripts/simulate-retries.mjs --attempts 8 --seed 7
```

| Attempt | Old delay | New ceiling |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| 1       | 500 ms    | 500 ms      |
| 4       | 4 s       | 4 s         |
| 8       | 64 s      | 30 s        |

> Backoff without a cap is a polite way of waiting forever.

The reasoning follows the [exponential backoff guide](https://example.com/docs/retries), which recommends full jitter for exactly this case.
Good catch. Fix the backoff, but keep the public API unchanged.
I'll patch the delay calculation in `backoff.ts` and run the suite.

streaming-half.anchor: the cap is enforced in nextdelay
streaming-half.text:
The cap is enforced in nextDelay: it takes the smaller of the exponential value and the ceiling, so a delay can never grow past thirty seconds.

The test I added checks three things:

1. at attempt 1 the delay stays under the base
2. at attempt 10 the delay never exceeds the cap
3. with a seeded random source the sequence is repeat

js: // the conversation's own status (a matching payload) is wiped first, so the only payload this tab ever hears is one that is NOT its own

if (ctx.cs.status.effort !== undefined || ctx.cs.status.model !== undefined || ctx.cs.status.contextWindow !== undefined) throw new Error('per-session fields were written from a payload that is not this tab\'s');
if (!ctx.cs.barParts.effort.seg.hidden) throw new Error('the effort must be hidden when no matching payload ever reported it');
if (ctx.cs.barParts.model.v.textContent !== 'Sonnet 5.5') throw new Error('the model must come from the transcript: ' + ctx.cs.barParts.model.v.textContent);
if (ctx.cs.status.fiveHourPct !== 42) throw new Error('the account-wide 5 h reading must still be taken');

setup: // The status-bar shots share one helper: pick the look, optionally narrow the pane, focus the box (so the keys hint shows), force one detail card open and
// FAIL the run if that card reaches into the composer or past the bar: the whole point of the card is that it never covers what is being typed.
if (o.pane) { ctx.p.el.style.flex = '0 0 auto'; ctx.p.el.style.width = o.pane + 'px'; ctx.p.el.style.alignSelf = 'flex-start'; }
const tip = r(seg.querySelector('.cb-tip')), bar = r(ctx.cs.bar), box = r(ctx.cs.box);
if (tip.top < box.bottom - 1.5) throw new Error('the detail card reaches into the composer');
if (tip.top < bar.top - 0.5 || tip.bottom > bar.bottom + 0.5 || tip.left < bar.left - 0.5 || tip.right > bar.right + 0.5) throw new Error('the detail card leaves the bar');
